result.topic_en: Ramanujan defines two quotients of series, U_n and V_n (related to powers of the eta function), states differential recurrences for them in terms of P, Q, R, and tabulates U_2 to U_10 and V_2 to V_10 as polynomials in P, Q, R.
result.transcription:

Add Ms a 94^{18 (110)}

I shall conclude this paper by considering two functions which can be expressed as polynomials in P, Q and R, viz.
$U_n = \frac{1^{n+1} - 3^{n+1}x + 5^{n+1}x^3 - 7^{n+1}x^6 + 9^{n+1}x^{10} - \cdots}{1 - 3x + 5x^3 - 7x^6 + 9x^{10} - \cdots}$,
$V_n = \frac{1^n - 5^n x - 7^n x^2 + 11^n x^5 + 13^n x^7 - \cdots}{1 - x - x^2 + x^5 + x^7 - \cdots}$,
where n is a positive even integer. It is easy to show that
$U_{n+2} = PU_n + 8x\frac{dU_n}{dx}$, $V_{n+2} = PV_n + 24x\frac{dV_n}{dx}$,
using the relations
$Q^3 - R^2 = 1728x(1 - 3x + 5x^3 - 7x^6 + \cdots)^8$
$= 1728x(1 - x - x^2 + x^5 + x^7 - \cdots)^{24}$.
It is evident that
$U_0 = V_0 = 1$.
From ( ) and ( ) we obtain the following results.
Table
1. $U_2 = P$. $V_2 = P$.
2. $U_4 = \frac{1}{3}(5P^2 - 2Q)$. $V_4 = 3P^2 - 2Q$.
3. $U_6 = \frac{1}{9}(35P^3 - 42PQ + 16R)$. $V_6 = 15P^3 - 30PQ + 16R$.
4. $\begin{cases} U_8 = \frac{1}{3}(35P^4 - 84P^2Q + 64PR - 12Q^2). \\ V_8 = 105P^4 - 420P^2Q + 448PR - 132Q^2. \end{cases}$
5. $\begin{cases} U_{10} = \frac{1}{9}(385P^5 - 1540P^3Q + 1760P^2R - 660PQ^2 + 64QR). \\ V_{10} = 945P^5 - 6300P^3Q + 10080P^2R - 5940PQ^2 + 1216QR. \end{cases}$
In general $U_{2s}$ and $V_{2s}$ are of the form
$\sum K_{l,m,n} P^l Q^m R^n$,
where $l + 2m + 3n = s$.
